subject: HK vendor onboarding: e-invoice samples, BR, and PO splitting for cross-border services
messages:
From: Michelle Chan <michelle.chan@muapp.hk>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: APAC Finance <apac-finance@partnerco.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:12:00 +0800
Subject: Vendor onboarding - documents and invoice format

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist. Attached are our Hong Kong BR (BR_certificate_muapp.pdf) and a sample invoice from MuApp HK (sample_invoice_muapp_hk.pdf). A couple of quick clarifications before we submit the full vendor form:

- We provide SaaS subscription services from MuApp Ltd. (Hong Kong), but for some customers in mainland China our invoices are issued by MuApp China (an affiliate). Will Redwood accept invoices from the China affiliate? If so, do we need to do anything special on the PO?
- Hong Kong does not have VAT/GST, but our China affiliate issues VAT invoices (fapiao). Do you have a preferred invoice format or fields we should use for cross-border billing?
- Finally, does Redwood require an e-invoice XML sample for automated AP ingestion? We can share an XML sample if helpful.

Attaching the BR and sample PDF; happy to provide bank details and any tax residency docs.

Best,
Michelle Chan
Head of Finance, MuApp Ltd.
michelle.chan@muapp.hk
+852 6123 4567

Attachments: BR_certificate_muapp.pdf, sample_invoice_muapp_hk.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Michelle Chan <michelle.chan@muapp.hk>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding - documents and invoice format

Hi Michelle — thanks for the files, they look good as a start. A few operational notes so we can map PO <> invoice correctly:

1) Entity on PO must match the remit entity for the invoice line items. If you will sometimes invoice from MuApp China please indicate which service lines come from CN vs HK so we can route POs accordingly. We typically create separate PO numbers per legal entity to avoid accounting splits later.

2) For Hong Kong invoices: correct, there is no VAT/GST — we just need the BR number, company registration name, and a local bank account for wire details.

3) For China-issued VAT invoices (fapiao): Finance requires a PDF of the fapiao and the raw XML if available. If the China entity will be charging VAT, include the VAT rate and taxpayer ID on the invoice.

4) Yes — an e-invoice XML sample is very helpful. Our AP system ingests the XML to automatically populate vendor, line items, tax fields, and VAT amounts. If you can attach an XML example that matches the fapiao fields, that will speed validation.

Next steps: can you confirm whether MuApp China will require its own PO (yes/no) and, if yes, which service SKUs map to that entity? Once we have that we’ll create two POs (HK / CN) and share the DocuSign vendor onboarding form for signature.

Thanks — looping in Ben and Laura from Finance for the tax mapping.

Best,
Priyom
Vendor Ops – Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: vendor_onboarding_form_redwood.docx (I will follow up with the DocuSign link)

Hi Priyom / Michelle,

Confirming MuApp China will occasionally issue invoices for managed services delivered in-country. For those invoices we will need the VAT fapiao and the underlying PO to reference the CN tax ID. For subscriptions delivered from HK, invoices will remain HK-origin and no VAT applies.

For integration: we can provide a sample Golden XML (China fapiao) and also a simplified eInvoice XML for HK/Singapore non-VAT invoices so Redwood's parser can handle both formats.

Let us know if Redwood requires separate vendor records for MUAPP-HK and MUAPP-CN — we generally expect that.

Regards,
APAC Finance (PartnerCo Group)
apac-finance@partnerco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michelle Chan <michelle.chan@muapp.hk>, APAC Finance <apac-finance@partnerco.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 17:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding - documents and invoice format

Hi Michelle / APAC Finance — quick guidance from Redwood AP/Tax: 

- Hong Kong: no VAT/GST. We only require the Business Registration (BR) and company legal name to populate our vendor master. Bank details and a PDF invoice are sufficient for payment routing.

- China invoices (fapiao): these must be treated as separate legal-entity invoices. We will require:
  * A separate vendor record for MuApp China (entity name + Chinese tax ID)
  * PDF of the fapiao and the underlying XML (Golden Fapiao) where possible
  * PO number that references the CN vendor record so tax reporting matches the recorded VAT input.

- Singapore (if relevant): for services invoiced into SG with GST charged, we need the GST registration number. If you are not GST-registered, Redwood does not expect to withhold anything but will request a declaration.

Operational recommendation: create two vendor records (MUAPP-HK / MUAPP-CN). For cross-border subscription items delivered from HK but billed via CN (rare), we will need a short memo explaining rationale and an intercompany agreement. That avoids misposting VAT.

Attached is a short XML sample (eInvoice_XML_sample.xml) with the fields our parser needs: vendor_tax_id, invoice_number, invoice_date, line_description, taxable_amount, tax_amount, currency. Please send a matching XML from MuApp China fapiao output if available.

If that all sounds good, we'll:
1) Create MUAPP-HK vendor record and open a PO for HK subscriptions.
2) If you confirm CN invoices, create MUAPP-CN vendor record and issue a separate PO for CN-managed services.
3) Send DocuSign onboarding packet for the HK vendor (link below).

Ben Carter
Sr. Accounting Manager — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: eInvoice_XML_sample.xml

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — agreed on the two-record approach. Michelle, can you: 

- Confirm which SKUs (subscription monthly / professional services / implementation) will be invoiced by MUAPP-CN vs MUAPP-HK? A quick table in reply is fine.
- Upload one sample Golden XML fapiao for the CN invoices and one non-VAT XML for HK to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz-samples) so AP can validate the parser.

I'll provision MUAPP-HK in the vendor master and draft the PO. Once we have the CN sample and tax ID we'll create MUAPP-CN and issue the second PO. I'll also start the DocuSign packet here: https://redwood.example.com/docusign/ABC-123 — please sign the vendor form so we can cut the PO.

If there are any special payment terms for CN (local currency, longer lead time), include that in your reply and we'll route to Treasury.

Best,
Laura Bennett

laura_bennett@redwood.ai
